questions.question: What does "master machine learning" mean for you in practice?
questions.why_it_matters: A mastery goal focused on deep understanding prioritizes math and derivations; a shipping goal prioritizes runnable pipelines and deployment patterns; a job-readiness goal adds portfolio pieces and interview topics; a product goal narrows scope to one working end-to-end service.

options.label: Deep understanding
options.implication: Adds derivations, loss-surface visualizations, and from-scratch implementations of optimizers and attention; deployment coverage is lighter.

options.label: Ship models fast
options.implication: Skips derivations; emphasizes template repos, CI/CD, feature stores, and monitoring; you leave with a production-ready scaffold you can extend.

options.label: Get hired as ML engineer
options.implication: Includes a portfolio-ready capstone (data → model → API → dashboard), system-design interview prep, and common take-home patterns.

options.label: Build a specific product
options.implication: Narrows the entire weekend to one problem domain (e.g., NLP classification, time-series forecasting, recommender); all tooling choices serve that domain.

questions.question: Which of these best describes your starting point?
questions.why_it_matters: A true beginner needs Python basics and ML vocabulary before touching frameworks; someone who has trained models in notebooks but never deployed needs the engineering layer; someone who has deployed once but hit scaling pain needs hardening patterns; an experienced engineer wanting a refresher can skip straight to modern tooling.

options.label: New to ML and Python
options.implication: Adds a Friday-evening Python crash course and supervised/unsupervised fundamentals; modeling day starts with a guided sklearn pipeline.

options.label: Comfortable with Python, have trained models in notebooks
options.implication: Skips basics; Saturday starts with experiment tracking, reproducible training loops, and model registry — the engineering layer you haven't used yet.

options.label: Have deployed once, hit scaling or reliability issues
options.implication: Compresses modeling; Sunday focuses on autoscaling, canary rollouts, drift detection, and cost optimization — the hardening layer.

options.label: Experienced engineer, want modern MLOps stack refresher
options.implication: Skips all code-along; delivers a decision matrix comparing Vertex AI, MLflow, Kubeflow, and managed services with migration checklists.

judgements.why: Essential first step - without framing the business problem as an ML task, nothing else matters. Weekend learner must start here.
Most production ML starts with tabular data. Python programmer can leverage pandas skills immediately.
Real data is messy. This is where Python proficiency pays off and where production models succeed/fail.
Highest ROI activity for tabular ML. Directly enables better models with same algorithms.
Non-negotiable for honest evaluation. Prevents the classic beginner mistake of testing on training data.
Required for reliable performance estimates with limited data. sklearn makes this accessible.
Must establish a baseline before complex modeling. Often beats complex models on tabular data.
Interpretable, fast, production-ready. Excellent baseline and often sufficient for production.
State-of-the-art for tabular data. XGBoost/LightGBM/CatBoost are production standards. Must include.
Cannot evaluate or improve what you cannot measure. Must match metrics to business problem.
Tree models need tuning. Optuna/scikit-optimize make this practical in hours, not days.
Bridge from notebook to production. joblib/MLflow basics are essential for deployment.
Architectural decision that shapes deployment. Learner must understand both patterns.
Concrete production deployment skill. FastAPI + Docker is the modern standard they can build in hours.
Production reality - models degrade. Basic monitoring (input distributions, prediction distributions) is achievable.
Overkill for first production model. Adds infrastructure complexity without immediate value at this scale.
Airflow/Prefect/Dagster are for recurring pipelines. Weekend project = single training run + deploy.
MLflow/Weights & Biases valuable for iteration cycles. One weekend = one focused experiment track.
GitHub Actions for model testing/deployment is real but secondary. Manual deploy first, automate later.
Tabular data dominates production ML. DL adds complexity (GPU, tuning, interpretability) with marginal gain here.

Specialized domain with unique patterns (embeddings, retrieval/ranking). Not generalizable first project.

Organizational framework, not technical skill. Learner needs hands-on building, not maturity assessment.

covered.why: First decision that shapes everything downstream. Learner converts a vague business ask into a concrete ML task (classification/regression, target, success metric).
Python programmer's entry point. Pandas profiling, dtypes, missingness, distributions, correlations — the lens they'll use for every dataset.
Real data is messy. Imputation, encoding, scaling, outlier handling — the hands-on steps that make or break production models.
Highest ROI activity for tabular ML. Interactions, datetime decomposition, target encoding, embeddings for high-cardinality categoricals.
Non-negotiable for honest evaluation. Time-based vs random, stratification, leakage prevention — the guardrails against fooling yourself.
Reliable performance estimates with limited data. K-fold, stratified, grouped CV — when each applies and how to use sklearn's tools.
Must beat a baseline before complex modeling. Mean/median for regression, majority class for regression, simple rules — often surprisingly strong.
Interpretable, fast, production-ready. Regularization (L1/L2), probability calibration, feature importance via coefficients — often sufficient for production.
State-of-the-art for tabular data. XGBoost/LightGBM/CatBoost usage, key hyperparameters, handling categoricals, early stopping — production standard.
Match metrics to business problem. Precision/recall/F1, ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, MAE/RMSE/RMSLE — and why accuracy is often the wrong choice.
Tree models need tuning. Optuna integration, search spaces, pruning, n_jobs — practical tuning in hours, not days.
Match metrics to business problem. Precision/recall/F1, ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, MAE/RMSE/RMSLE — and why accuracy is often the wrong choice.
Bridge from notebook to production. joblib/pickle/MLflow model format, versioning, metadata (training data hash, metrics, params) — deployable artifact.
Architectural decision shaping deployment. Batch (scheduled, high-throughput) vs online (low-latency, request-response) — tradeoffs and when each fits.
Concrete production skill. FastAPI + Pydantic for validation, Dockerfile, health checks, graceful startup/shutdown — runnable container in hours.
Production reality — models degrade. Input distribution monitoring (PSI, KS test), prediction distribution shifts, performance proxy metrics — actionable alerts.

modules.title: Foundations: Problem Framing & Data Understanding
modules.why_here: The two concepts that must precede all others: defining what you're solving and understanding the raw material. Both are exploration-heavy, code-light, and set the frame for every downstream decision.
modules.capability: Convert a vague business problem into a concrete ML task definition (target, task type, success metric) and produce a data profile report covering distributions, missingness, correlations, and data quality issues

modules.title: Data Preparation: Cleaning, Preprocessing & Feature Engineering
modules.why_here: Both are hands-on data transformation steps that feed directly into modeling. They share the same pandas/sklearn toolchain and the same 'fit on train, transform on test' discipline. Splitting them would fragment the preprocessing pipeline.
modules.capability: Build a reusable preprocessing pipeline (imputation, encoding, scaling, datetime features, interaction features, target encoding) that fits on training data and transforms validation/test without leakage

modules.title: Modeling: Baselines, Linear Models & Tree-Based Models
modules.why_here: Complete modeling stack from validation strategy through baseline to production-grade models. All use sklearn/XGBoost/LightGBM APIs. The split strategy and CV are prerequisites for honest model comparison; baselines, linear, and tree models form the progression from simple to state-of-the-art for tabular data.
modules.capability: Train, compare, and select among baseline, linear, and gradient-boosted tree models using proper train/validation/test splits and cross-validation, with a reproducible training script that outputs a serialized model artifact

modules.title: Evaluation & Iteration: Metrics, Cross-Validation & Hyperparameter Tuning
modules.why_here: Metrics define what 'good' means; tuning finds the best configuration. Both are iteration-loop activities — you evaluate, tune, re-evaluate. They belong together because tuning optimizes for a specific metric, and metric choice changes tuning outcomes.
modules.capability: Select and justify evaluation metrics aligned to the business problem, then run hyperparameter optimization (Optuna) targeting that metric to produce a tuned model with documented performance

modules.title: Production: Serialization, Serving, API Deployment & Monitoring
modules.why_here: End-to-end production path: artifact → serving pattern → API container → monitoring. Each step consumes the previous. Batch vs online is the architectural fork; the API module implements online; monitoring closes the loop. One coherent deployment narrative.
modules.capability: Package a trained model as a versioned artifact, choose and justify a serving pattern (batch vs online), deploy an online inference API with FastAPI + Docker (health checks, input validation, logging), and implement basic data drift monitoring on input features and predictions

sequence: Day 1 Morning: Problem Framing & Data Preparation
output.why: Three-session progressive build matching a two-day calendar. Morning/afternoon split on Day 1 respects cognitive load; Day 2 is the deployment sprint. Each session produces a working artifact the next consumes.

modules.title: Day 1 Morning: Problem Framing & Data Preparation
modules.why_here: All data-side work in one block: define the task, understand the data, clean it, engineer features, split it properly. Shared pandas/sklearn toolchain. ~3.5 hours.
modules.capability: Convert a business problem into a concrete ML task definition and produce a clean, feature-rich training/validation/test split ready for modeling, with a reusable preprocessing pipeline that prevents leakage

modules.title: Day 1 Afternoon: Modeling & Evaluation
modules.why_here: Complete modeling loop: establish baseline, train production-grade tree models, evaluate with business-aligned metrics, tune hyperparameters. All sklearn/XGBoost/Optuna. ~3.5 hours.
modules.capability: Train, evaluate, and tune a gradient-boosted tree model (XGBoost/LightGBM/CatBoost) against a proper baseline using business-aligned metrics, with a reproducible training script that outputs a serialized model artifact

modules.title: Day 2: Production Deployment & Monitoring
modules.why_here: End-to-end production path: artifact -> serving choice -> API container -> monitoring. Each step consumes the previous. One coherent deployment narrative. ~3-4 hours.
modules.capability: Package a trained model as a versioned artifact, choose and justify a serving pattern (batch vs online), deploy an online inference API with FastAPI + Docker (health checks, input validation, logging), and implement basic data drift monitoring on input features and predictions

judgements.why: Essential first step - without framing the business problem as an ML task, nothing else matters. Weekend learner must start here.
Most production ML starts with tabular data. Python programmer can leverage pandas skills immediately.
Real data is messy. This is where Python proficiency pays off and where production models succeed/fail.
Highest ROI activity for tabular ML. Directly enables better models with same algorithms.
Non-negotiable for honest evaluation. Prevents the classic beginner mistake of testing on training data.
Required for reliable performance estimates with limited data. sklearn makes this accessible.
Must establish a baseline before complex modeling. Often beats complex models on tabular data.
Interpretable, fast, production-ready. Excellent baseline and often sufficient for production.
State-of-the-art for tabular data. XGBoost/LightGBM/CatBoost are production standards. Must include.
Cannot evaluate or improve what you cannot measure. Must match metrics to business problem.
Tree models need tuning. Optuna/scikit-optimize make this practical in hours, not days.
Bridge from notebook to production. joblib/MLflow basics are essential for deployment.
Architectural decision that shapes deployment. Learner must understand both patterns.
Concrete production deployment skill. FastAPI + Docker is the modern standard they can build in hours.
Production reality - models degrade. Basic monitoring (input distributions, prediction distributions) is achievable.
Overkill for first production model. Adds infrastructure complexity without immediate value at this scale.
Airflow/Prefect/Dagster are for recurring pipelines. Weekend project = single training run + deploy.
MLflow/Weights & Biases valuable for iteration cycles. One weekend = one focused experiment track.
GitHub Actions for model testing/deployment is real but secondary. Manual deploy first, automate later.
Tabular data dominates production ML. DL adds complexity (GPU, tuning, interpretability) with marginal gain here.

judgements.concept: Neural Network Architectures (MLP, CNN, RNN, Transformer)
judgements.why: Architecture selection is a deep topic. Not needed for tabular baseline -> production path.
Relevant for unstructured data (NLP/vision). Out of scope for tabular-focused weekend.
Requires entirely different tooling (tokenizers, CV transforms, audio processing). Weekend too short.
Specialized domain with unique patterns (embeddings, retrieval/ranking). Not generalizable first project.
Specialized validation (walk-forward), features (lags, windows), metrics. Deserves its own weekend.
Organizational framework, not technical skill. Learner needs hands-on building, not maturity assessment.

covered.why: First decision that shapes everything. Convert vague ask into concrete ML task (classification/regression, target, success metric) in 30 minutes.
Pandas profiling, dtypes, missingness, distributions, correlations — the lens for every dataset. 45 minutes.
Imputation, encoding, scaling, outlier handling — the hands-on steps that make or break production models. 90 minutes.
Highest ROI for tabular ML. Datetime decomposition, interactions, target encoding for high-cardinality categoricals. 60 minutes.
Time-based vs random, stratification, leakage prevention. Non-negotiable for honest evaluation. 30 minutes.
Must beat a baseline. Mean/median for regression, majority class for classification, simple rules. 30 minutes.
State-of-the-art for tabular data. XGBoost/LightGBM/CatBoost usage, key hyperparameters, early stopping. 90 minutes.
Match metrics to business problem. Precision/recall/F1, ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, MAE/RMSE — why accuracy is often wrong. 60 minutes.
Show Optuna integration, search spaces, pruning — practical tuning in 30 minutes, not hours. Learner runs one tuning job.
Bridge from notebook to production. joblib/MLflow model format, versioning, metadata (data hash, metrics, params). 45 minutes.
Architectural fork: batch (scheduled, high-throughput) vs online (low-latency, request-response). Choose one for the weekend. 20 minutes.
Concrete production skill. FastAPI + Pydantic validation, Dockerfile, health checks, logging — runnable container in 2 hours.
Production reality — models degrade. Input distribution monitoring (PSI), prediction shifts, performance proxies. 30 minutes.
